title: Optimizing Generalized Rate Metrics with Three Players
authors: Harikrishna Narasimhan, Andrew Cotter, Maya Gupta (Maya R. Gupta per DBLP)
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), vol. 32
conclusions: Presents a three-player game framework (theta-player, xi-player, lambda-player) for optimizing/constraining general non-linear functions of classification rates (e.g. F-measure, G-mean, KL-divergence, predictive parity, churn), generalizing prior two-player Lagrangian game approaches.

Decouples the non-linear rate objective from the rates themselves via auxiliary variables xi, enabling each player to use a different optimization strategy (best response, online gradient descent, follow-the-leader).

Gives convergence guarantees (approximate Nash / coarse-correlated equilibrium) for convex objectives and constraints that are functions of rates, extending prior linear-rate-constraint results and resolving an open convergence question from Cotter et al.
Extends the framework with a heuristic algorithm (Algorithm 3) for objectives/constraints that are sums-of-ratios of rates (e.g. predictive parity, F-measure parity).

All bounds/guarantees are stated on the model's EXPECTED rate R(theta;D) = E[1{Y=sign(f(X))}] over a data distribution D -- i.e. inductive, population-level rate constraints -- not on hard counts over a fixed, finite test/transductive set.

Experiments (fairness/rate-constrained classification on COMPAS, Communities&Crime, Law School, Adult, Wiki Toxicity) show the method satisfies KL-divergence and F-measure-parity constraints better than unconstrained/plug-in baselines.
our_use: main.tex:184, in the 'Rate-constrained learning' related-work paragraph: '...and generalized rate metrics through multi-player schemes \citep{narasimhan2019optimizing}. These bound expected rates over a distribution, inductively. Our requirement is a hard count on one specific test set: transductive, verified on the argmax predictions themselves, and paired with per-group local caps.' -- cited as an example of classical rate-constrained learning that bounds EXPECTED rates inductively, contrasted with TraLO's transductive hard-count-on-argmax setting.
